newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures end short session lower.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures end short session lower.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended an abbreviated trading session mostly lower after moderately active range trading.
Exchange price boards showed estimated volume in March yen, marks and Swiss francs of about 15,000, 13,000 and 12,000 contracts, respectively, during the shortened day.
But order flows dwindled as traders cautiously approached the long U.S. weekend. Currency futures closed two hours early Friday and will stay shut Monday for Presidents Day.
Brokers said sentiment remained dollar-bullish but intervention jitters limited the downside.
"Everyone's been sitting on their hands," said one floor broker late in the session. "It (weekend) would be a good time to intervene, so nobody wants to take a position home."
They said a further dollar rise above 125.00 yen and 1.70 marks might provoke central banks to sell dollars. Those levels are roughly equal to $0.008031 in March yen and $0.5892 in nearby marks.
"That is the waiting game," said another floor broker.
"Next week we should see some more (dollar) follow-through on the upside," added a third broker, citing 1.70 and 125.00 as levels he expected to easily achieve.

"We're going to get there," a floor analyst said of 125.00 yen. "It's just a question of whether it's today or next week (and)...whether people start booking profits at these levels just in case the Fed does intervene."

Futures firmed after January U.S. producer prices fell 0.3 percent against forecasts for a 0.3 percent increase. The core rate, which excludes the volatile food and energy components, was unchanged compared to expectations for a 0.2 percent rise.
Currencies moved little on further soft U.S. data. January industrial output was flat and capacity use dipped to 83.3 percent versus forecasts for up 0.1 percent and 83.4 percent.

Some looked for a return of volatile trading conditions next week, which will be littered with U.S. and German economic data. The figures include fourth-quarter German M3 money supply and the Ifo business climate index, and U.S. December trade balance and consumer price index data.
March yen and Swiss francs each set new contract lows Friday, while nearby marks flirted with its contract low.

March yen rose $0.000014 to $0.008082, mark off $0.0012 at $0.5938, Swiss fr fell $0.0044 to $0.6850, pound off $0.0032 to $1.6200, Can dollar rose $0.0003 to $0.7418, Aussie dollar lost $0.0002 to $0.7657, Mex peso rose $0.000425 to $0.127125.
